compare_countries.description: Put several countries side by side on one chart, ranked largest first, each with its share of their combined total and how far it is behind the leader. Every country is read at its own most recent year, because statistical agencies publish on their own schedules and insisting on one shared year would silently drop whoever had not reported yet. Anything the chart does not cover is reported as missing rather than quietly left out. No account or API key required.

find_articles.description: Search what Our World in Data writes rather than what it charts: research articles, the short daily data insights, and the topic pages that explain a subject end to end. description: Put the world's research data into a workflow. Our World in Data collects what the UN, the World Bank, the WHO, the IHME and a few hundred other institutions publish on how the world is changing - life expectancy, emissions, poverty, energy, health, education - puts every country on the same names and the same years, and publishes one chart per question. Search those charts by subject, or describe what you need in plain English and let it find the indicator that means it. Then read the numbers: one country's latest figure for a sentence in an email, a run of years for a report, several countries ranked side by side, or the top and bottom of the world. Take a picture of any chart to put in a message, and get the line that credits its sources back with every answer, because all of it is CC BY and asks to be cited. Every action reads: nothing here changes anything. No account or API key required.
